did_you_know.text: Did you know? Saul chose a small army of 3,000 men: 2,000 were with him at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and 1,000 were with Jonathan at Gibeah of Benjamin. He sent the rest of the people home.
Did you know? Jonathan was the one who attacked the Philistine garrison at Geba, while Saul blew the trumpet to announce it throughout the land and summon the Hebrews.
Did you know? The Philistines assembled for battle with a massive force: 30,000 chariots, 6,000 horsemen, and troops as numerous as the sand on the seashore.
Did you know? Because of the military pressure, the Israelites hid in caves, thickets, among the rocks, in pits, and in cisterns.
Did you know? Saul waited seven days for the time appointed by Samuel, but when Samuel did not arrive and the people began to scatter, Saul decided to offer the burnt offering himself.
Did you know? Saul explained his actions to Samuel by citing three factors: the people were scattering, Samuel was late, and the Philistines were gathering at Michmash.

Did you know? Samuel viewed Saul’s offering of the burnt offering as disobedience to the LORD’s command and told him that his kingdom would not endure. He said that the LORD had sought out a man after his own heart.
Did you know? After Samuel left, Saul had only about 600 men remaining with him, even though he had chosen 3,000 warriors at the beginning of the chapter.

Did you know? According to the chapter, there was no blacksmith anywhere in the land of Israel because the Philistines feared that the Israelites would make swords and spears. Therefore, the Israelites had to go to the Philistines to sharpen and repair their farm tools.
Did you know? On the day of the battle, none of the people had a sword or spear; only Saul and Jonathan had such weapons.
